comments.text: isNonDeliverableIdentity is not a sound fix. strings.Contains(identity, "test") matches any identity containing 'test' anywhere (e.g. contest@gmail.com, testing.team@company.com, latest@corp.io), which are real deliverable mailboxes, so email lookups no longer keep their priority for them and the other identity fields (e.g. username) are also searched. That lets a user whose username equals someone else's email-like identity collide with/shadow that account depending on loop ordering, and the behavior depends on an arbitrary substring rather than the actual issue. The real bug (email-like usernames not found when the email field doesn't match) is already covered by the existing `foundErr != nil` fallback; if something else is broken, fix it generally (e.g. fall back to other identity fields only when the email lookup found nothing) rather than via a hardcoded domain/substring allowlist. Also no tests were added for the new behavior.
